Code: panels/layers/index.tsx:405-411 renders LayerSelectionBanner whenever 2+ are selected — Group / Dim in editor / Delete / Done (LayerSelectionBanner.tsx:35-67) — and index.tsx:412-418 renders the inline 'Delete N layers?' confirm.

finding: The reorder the board draws is not the reorder the code performs: the drop index is decremented twice, so a same-parent downward drag lands one slot too high and the adjacent case (drop just below your neighbour) does nothing at all.
evidence: Board 143:60 draws the insertion line BELOW the dragged 'Button' row (R 'insertion line' @0,192 280x2, ghosted row @0,164). Code: panels/layers/index.tsx:156-166 computes dropIndex = targetIndex+1 for 'after', then subtracts 1 when sourceIndex < dropIndex; engine/elements/manager/ElementCRUD.ts:183-189 subtracts 1 again for the same-parent case (its pre-removal convention is pinned by engine/elements/__tests__/ElementManager.crud.test.ts 'adjusts the index on a same-parent FORWARD move' — moveElement(a,root,2) => [b,a,c]). [A,B,C] dropping A after B therefore calls moveElement(A,root,1) -> engine adjusts to 0 -> order unchanged. No test covers the panel drop path (no dataTransfer/onDrop test under editor/panels/layers).
fix: Delete the panel-side adjustment at index.tsx:158-163 and pass the raw pre-removal slot (targetIndex or targetIndex+1); add a drop-order test for before/after/inside in both directions.

finding: Two of the three drop positions have no board: only a sibling insertion line is drawn, so nesting — the thing the shipped copy tells users to do — has never been designed.
evidence: 143:60's only drop cue is R 'insertion line' @0,192 280x2 (fetched); no parent highlight, no indent cue, no aiming zones. panels/layers/types.ts:56 defines 'before' | 'after' | 'inside'; index.tsx:248-261 splits a 28px row 30% / 40% / 30% and only offers 'inside' when canHaveChildren(type); index.tsx:388 ships the line 'Every element on this page. Drag a row to reorder or nest it.'
fix: Add 'Layers · drop-inside' from 143:60: container row outlined as the drop target, the dragged row ghosted, and the 30/40/30 aim bands annotated so the 8px middle zone is a decision, not an accident.

finding: The context menu's only two prototype links point at modals for actions the menu has no item for — and both links sit outside the board's own bounds, so they cannot fire at all.
evidence: Fetched 1082:4527: none of its nine items (Cut, Copy, Paste, Duplicate, Delete, Rename, Group selection, [not-implemented] Move to page…, Copy link) carries a reaction; its only state links are two hotspot frames at y820 -> 1706:8501 'Modal · Add Child Element' and -> 1170:4777 'Components · create (modal)'. The board is 812 tall with clipsContent=true (fetched), so both hotspots are clipped away. Inbound scan of the page edge dump: 1706:8501 is reached from 1082:4527 and nothing else, and it is absent from packages/editor/scripts/conformance/boards.json. Neither action exists in the shipped menu (LayerContextMenu.tsx:61-101): add-child is BlockPickerModal (canvas/controls/BlockPickerModal.tsx:19-26, position 'child'|'before'|'after') opened only from UnifiedSelectionToolbar.tsx:322, and create-component is emitted only from sidebar/LeftSidebar.tsx:528 and refuses without a canvas selection (:511-527).
fix: Add 'Add child element…' and 'Create component…' as real items on 1082:4527 and in LayerContextMenu.tsx, and move the two reactions onto those items, inside the frame. A layer row is the natural place to insert inside a container the canvas cannot click.

finding: There is no way back out of a successful search: the filtered board draws no clear control, and the shipped search input has none either — 'Clear search' exists only in the no-results state.

finding: Deleting a subtree from Layers is silent and unconfirmed, and the one datum that would justify a confirmation is computed and thrown away.
evidence: useLayersState.ts:151 sets childCount: countDescendants(node) on every context-menu open; LayerContextMenu.tsx:11-21 does not take childCount, so nothing renders it. useLayerActions.ts:208-217 deleteLayer runs removeElement inside a transaction with no confirm and no toast; the canvas path for the same act shows '<name> (N children) deleted' with an Undo action (canvas/hooks/useCanvasKeyboard.ts:198,212-230). The board draws Delete as a plain row with no consequence state.

finding: A layer name — and hidden and locked with it — is stored per browser, not in the site, so a rename does not survive a different device, a different browser or a cleared cache. Nothing on any board says so.
evidence: layersPersistence.ts:15-22 keys everything as 'buildrick-layers-<pageId>-{hidden,locked,names}' in localStorage; useLayerActions.ts:110-125 persists the three there and hydrates them at :70-96. saveEditedName (useLayerActions.ts:180-201) writes only the customNames map and emits ELEMENT_RENAMED; no element or project field is written (the tree itself is rebuilt from engine elements, useLayerTree.ts:88-97, which carries no name).
fix: Persist the layer name on the element (and hidden/locked with it) so it exports and syncs, or state on the board that these are personal view settings. A name a collaborator cannot see is a different feature from the one the panel implies.

finding: While filtering, the footer reports the whole tree instead of the match count, on the board and in the code.

fix: Footer contract for all six list states: 'n of m' while filtering, count while idle, skeleton while loading, absent on failure.

finding: Hiding is drawn as row opacity with the same 👁 glyph on every row, and the sentence that stops a user mistaking it for 'hide from my published site' is on no board.

Publishing is governed elsewhere (the inspector's Visibility section).
fix: Draw the eye-off glyph on the hidden row and put the 'still publishes' line on 143:179 as a tooltip or footnote — this is the module's highest-consequence ambiguity.

finding: Locking a layer has no drawn outcome: the 'locked' board is visually indistinguishable from the tree at rest, so the board does not tell a user the lock took, nor what a locked row can no longer do.

Code changes several things at once: the row loses drag (canDrag = composer && depth>0 && !isLocked, LayerTreeItem.tsx:99,173), gains ', locked' in its aria-label and '(Locked)' in its title (:176,178), F2/double-click rename is refused (:146,196), and the engine element is locked (useLayerActions.ts:161-168).
fix: Redraw 143:237 with a filled/closed padlock, the muted row treatment, and a note that a locked row cannot be dragged or renamed — otherwise the state exists only in code.

finding: The board named for renaming does not draw a rename: the row keeps its old label inside a 2px focus ring, with no input, no caret, no selected text and no commit or cancel affordance.
evidence: Fetched 1082:4589: seven plain Tree rows, labels 'Section' … 'Footer', no input/field node anywhere in the subtree; the screenshot shows the 'Heading' row outlined in accent blue and still reading 'Heading'. finding: No board shows the panel the way it actually stacks: every board starts the tree at y80, but the shipped panel always reserves an ancestor-crumb band and a purpose line above it, so every row position measured off these boards is wrong.

Drag a row to reorder or nest it.' (index.tsx:386-390), then the selection banner, then the tree. finding: 'Show in Layers' — the answer to an element the canvas cannot click — has no arrival board: nothing shows the tree scrolled to, expanded to and selecting the revealed row.

finding: The module's only error board cannot be built from: the rule is clipped mid-sentence and a layout annotation is drawn over the tree rows.

F 'bdc-layers-crumb' @0,80 280x32 holds the note '(empty slot — reserved so selecting a row cannot reflow the tree)' and sits on top of 'Tree row' @0,80. The board also shows no drop line, so the rejected target is not identified. finding: The loading board prints a layer count it cannot know, and the code prints a different wrong one.
evidence: Fetched 775:4130: seven skeleton rows and footer TEXT '12 layers' @12,790. 781:4217 and 782:4260 print no footer at all. Code drops the count only on tree failure — 'a count of a list that did not load is not a fact' (LayersTab.tsx:212-222) — and during loading the same footer renders stats.total, which is 0 until the tree builds.
fix: Apply the code's own rule to the loading state: no count, or a skeleton in the footer.

finding: The empty state fires in a state its copy does not describe: the tree is never empty for an empty page, so 'This page is empty' can only appear when there is no page or no composer.
evidence: Fetched 143:355 (frame name self-labels UNBUILDABLE): 'This page is empty. Drop something on the canvas to see it here.' + 'Open Insert', footer '0 layers'. useLayerTree.ts:97 always emits the page root as row 0 and returns [] only when composer, page or root element is missing (:58-72); index.tsx:431 renders LayersEmptyState on layers.length === 0 and LayersEmptyState.tsx:20-33 ships this exact copy — so the shipped footer reads '1 layer' for an empty page and this screen shows up only with no page open.
fix: Re-word for the state it actually reaches ('No page open') or exclude the root row from the tree so the drawn state becomes reachable; then drop the UNBUILDABLE label. Same finding as D-F-22, restated here because it breaks the entry step of every Layers job on a new site.

finding: DEAD by stacking — three walk hotspots are painted underneath larger ones, so 'back to editor' survives as a 4px sliver on two boards and 'no-results' is completely buried on the tree board.

finding: DEAD — every item in the right-click menu is bare text with nothing behind it, including Rename, which has its own board, and Delete, which has no consequence board at all.

finding: Rows fit their controls, but three of the four per-row controls are drawn below the 20px minimum hit target the founder set for editor chrome — the expand chevron is 4px wide on every board.
evidence: Hand sweep (v2's 40-260px window cannot see icon buttons). 143-family rows are 28 tall with T '▾' 4x16 @12/22, T '👁' 10x16 @238, T '🔒' 10x16 @254 (142:2, 143:2, 143:60, 143:119, 143:179, 143:237, 143:295, 1171:4829). 1082-family rows: '▾' 4x12, '👁' 10x10 @246, '🔒' 10x10 @262 (1082:4527, 4589, 4640, 4739, 4835).
